messages:
maya (sec-eng): Heads-up — we're planning a cross-cloud KEK rotation + data rewrap next quarter (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Need input on auto-rotate vs manual rewrap, RBAC changes, audit hooks, and an incident/rollback play if rewrap fails.

alex (infra): +1. Important to separate KEK rotation (rotate CMK) from ciphertext rewrap. In many clouds rotating the CMK metadata is cheap but existing ciphertext still references old KEK unless re-encrypted.

raj (sre): Question on runtime: will rewrap be streaming (on read) or bulk offline? streaming avoids big batch jobs but spikes latency and load. bulk gives predictable window.

maya (sec-eng): Thinking hybrid: canary bulk rewrap for a subset, then scheduled background workers for the rest. Have a short streaming fallback for cold objects on first read.

alex (infra): For AWS: two common approaches — 1) Use KMS GenerateDataKey+Encrypt workflow and re-encrypt object ciphertexts with new data key wrapped by new CMK; 2) Use AWS re-encrypt API (kms:ReEncrypt) where supported. Example pseudo-command: ```aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://obj.ct --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:...```

alex (infra): GCP and Azure don't have a single re-encrypt API equivalent; we'll need a worker that: decrypts with old KEK (via KMS), re-encrypts with new KEK, and writes new envelope (update header).

maya (sec-eng): Important: include explicit header version and key-id/kek-version in ciphertext header so we can always tell which KEK to call for decrypt. Otherwise rolling back is painful.

sophie (platform): RBAC: rewrap workers only need decrypt with old KEK and encrypt with new KEK, plus write to object store. Principle of least privilege -> create ephemeral service account per rollout with policy: `kms:Decrypt`, `kms:Encrypt` on specific key ARNs, `s3:PutObject`/`Storage.objects.update` limited prefix. Revoke at end.

maya (sec-eng): Also require IAM review for cross-project/key access. Document temporary elevation steps in case we need emergency rollback.

raj (sre): Observability: emit metrics for rewrap success/failure per object, bytes/sec, failure_reason labels. Add a rewrap-run audit event to our central audit log with fields: object_id, old_kek_id, new_kek_id, actor, duration, status. Need trace id to link to request.

security-bot: Ticket created: SEC-ROT-3141 — "Cross-cloud KEK rotation runbook + RBAC + audit". Assigned: maya, alex, raj. :white_check_mark:

oncall-ops: If a worker hits widespread `AccessDenied` we should auto-pause and open an incident channel. Plan: circuit-breaker at X failures per minute and feature-flagged rollback job that reinstates previous envelope header mapping.

alex (infra): Rollout timing: slice by object age / heat. Start with low-heat objects in eu-west-1 for canary, then expand. Limit bandwidth to avoid saturating egress. Schedule during low-traffic windows for each region.

maya (sec-eng): Backwards compatibility: runtime decryptors must accept both v1 and v2 envelope formats. Keep old KEKs available until 2 releases after rollout. Add lint check to prevent producing v2 without header.

sophie (platform): Vulnerability triage: if a crypto CVE requires emergency rewrap, we need an "urgent" path with pre-approved runbook and elevated RBAC that is audited heavily. Also pre-generate rewrap worker images and infra templates.

raj (sre): Incident response: add runbook steps: pause rewrap, revert service-account, restore object pointers, trigger oncall, snapshot object-store prefix, run dry-run decrypts on sample objects.

maya (sec-eng): One more thing — telemetry: log counts to BigQuery + alert if error_rate > 0.5% for 15m. We'll need dashboards.

alex (infra): Small policy snippet for AWS role (example): ```{ "Version":"2012-10-17", "Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:ReEncrypt"],"Resource":["arn:aws:kms:...:key/OLD","arn:aws:kms:...:key/NEW"]}]}``` Keep scope to specific key ARNs and S3 prefixes.

maya (sec-eng): Action items: 1) alex: draft rewrap worker design + cloud-specific differences (due EOW). 2) sophie: RBAC matrix and temporary escalation policy. 3) raj: observability + circuit-breaker thresholds. 4) maya: runbook + audit schema.

sophie (platform): I'll start the RBAC matrix and link to SEC-ROT-3141.

raj (sre): I'll prototype a small canary rewrap in staging and report perf impact.

maya (sec-eng): Great. Ping me if you need key ARNs. We'll sync Tues 10am. :calendar:
